assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, and Reset are modeled as parent-scoped events rather than persistent input variables, because the NL describes them as triggers/signals.
hbrg is encoded as an integer output with 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop.
The NL does not specify priority when multiple floor requests are present simultaneously, so no additional arbitration behavior is invented.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: The automatic elevator controller is built as a finite-state machine
state space combines floor states F1, F2, and F3

state space combines floor states F1, F2, and F3
motion states MU2, MU3, MD1, and MD2 for upward and downward travel

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init verifies start at F1 stopped, no-request no-fire, F1 PS2 upward to MU2, arrival at F2, then next PS1 request downward to F1.
scenario_results.name: default_init_f1_f2_then_down_to_f1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies F1 PS3 chooses direct upward MU3, S3 stops at F3, and Reset from a floor context forces F1.
scenario_results.name: f1_direct_to_f3_and_reset_from_floor

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies PS3 from F2 transitions to upward MU3 and S3 arrival stops at F3.
scenario_results.name: f2_to_f3_upward_request

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies PS1 from F3 transitions to downward MD1 and S1 arrival stops at F1.
scenario_results.name: f3_to_f1_downward_request

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies PS2 from F3 transitions to downward MD2 and S2 arrival stops at F2.
scenario_results.name: f3_to_f2_downward_request

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies the forced Reset rule from an upward motion state returns to F1 and stop output.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_upward_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start verifies the forced Reset rule from a downward motion state returns to F1 and stop output.
scenario_results.name: reset_from_downward_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start probes that MU3 only completes on S3, so an S2 arrival signal must not stop the upward-to-F3 motion.
scenario_results.name: wrong_arrival_sensor_does_not_complete_motion

evidence: NL requires floor states F1/F2/F3 and motion states MU2/MU3/MD1/MD2; DSL defines all seven leaf states.
NL requires F1->MU2 on PS2, F1->MU3 on PS3, F2->MU3 on PS3, F2->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD1 on PS1, F3->MD2 on PS2; DSL contains these transitions.
NL requires MU2+S2->F2, MU3+S3->F3, MD1+S1->F1, MD2+S2->F2; DSL contains these transitions.
NL states reset forces controller back to floor 1; DSL has '! * -> F1 : Reset'.
findings.summary: The DSL is broadly faithful to the explicit NL state space, request-triggered movement transitions, arrival-sensor completion transitions, hbrg direction/stop output, initial state, and forced reset behavior.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary reports 7 leaf states, 7 events, 1 variable, and 18 total transitions including forced reset expansion.
GroundingMap includes required entries for all states, all PS/S/Reset events, all explicit NL transitions, and hbrg actions for stop/up/down.
findings.summary: Core components are covered: states, events, transitions, reset, and hbrg output actions are all represented.

evidence: NL says reset forces the controller back to floor 1 'regardless of the outstanding request context'.
GroundingMap assumption says no priority/arbitration behavior is invented because NL does not specify priority when multiple floor requests are present simultaneously.
DSL models PS1/PS2/PS3 as events only and contains no request-memory variables.
findings.summary: The DSL does not model persistent outstanding requests or request arbitration; this is probably acceptable under the provided assumptions, but it leaves the phrase 'outstanding request context' and simultaneous/multiple request behavior underspecified.

evidence: DSL contains each named state and each explicit transition from the NL.
hbrg is assigned on state entry to represent stop/up/down conditions.
findings.summary: No blocking over-simplification is evident; the model is intentionally a simple event-driven FSM matching the explicit transition table.

evidence: NL: 'A reset signal forces the controller back to floor 1 regardless of the outstanding request context.'
DSL: '! * -> F1 : Reset;'
findings.summary: Reset-to-F1 from any state is not flagged as unsafe recovery here because it is directly required by the NL, although physical elevator designs would normally require additional safety constraints not present in the NL.

evidence: inspect_model_to_json_summary reports n_transitions_forced = 7.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports n_variables = 1 and all transition guards are null in the sample.
findings.summary: The forced reset wildcard is expanded by inspection into forced transitions from all leaf states; this is structurally acceptable, but the design has minimal internal data and no guards, so behavioral richness is limited to event transitions.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary has blocking_count = 0 and one advisory W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg.
NL describes hbrg as an output distinguishing upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
findings.summary: No unjustified warning fix is present. The unreferenced hbrg warning is advisory and hbrg is plausibly an output variable rather than a guard variable.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary ok = true with blocking_count = 0.
sim_summary ok = true with 8 of 8 scenarios passed.
GroundingMap required elements are represented in the DSL.
No blocking diagnostics or empty-shell pattern is evident.
findings.summary: Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate. No quality cap is applied because required states, transitions, events, and hbrg actions are present, simulations pass, and the only diagnostic is an advisory output-variable warning.
